ended: Lost the West 1st Round 2-4 to MIN

archetype.name: Early Playoff Exit (offense-only contender)
archetype.definition: A 54-win team with the league's best offense and a bottom-third defense that rode a perfect finish into the playoffs and then lost its first-round series to Minnesota in six games when the shooting left.

report.headline: League's best offense, a 10-0 finish, then six games of missed shots

recap.finish: 54-28, second in the Northwest; lost the West 1st Round 2-4 to MIN
recap.body:
This was Denver's most lopsided team of the recent run. The offense was the best in basketball at a 122.6 rating, leading the league in eFG % (57.7), TS % (61.6) and 3P % (39.6), with the third-lowest TOV % and the fourth-best FT Rate. The defense ranked 21st at 117.4 and forced turnovers less than any team in the league (Opp TOV % 10.4, 30th). The Net Rtg of 5.2, seventh in the league, describes a good team rather than a great one, and the 54 wins matched the margin almost exactly: W vs Pt Diff was +1 against 53 wins by differential. There was no close-game luck to give back. The record was earned, and it is also about where it should have been.

The season came in three acts. November (11-3) set the tone. December and January stayed on the winning side, but the defense leaked 122 points a game in December, and January was the one month the offense sputtered, at 109.81 a game. February was the low point at 4-7, the only losing month. Then the team took off: 11-5 in March and 6-0 in April, closing on a 10-0 run and a season-best 12-game winning streak. Two of those last ten went to overtime and a couple more were two-point games, but the stretch still outscored opponents by 10.5 a game. Beating OKC 127-107 and San Antonio twice in the final week made the run look real.

Nikola Jokić was the engine, and the gap between him and everyone else defined the roster. His 14.2 BPM, 14.9 Win Shares and 67 TS % made the frontcourt grade a B+, and the team was 13.5 points per 100 better with him on the floor. He played 65 games. Jamal Murray earned All-NBA Third Team with 9.5 Win Shares. Beyond those two, the backcourt and wings both graded C+. Aaron Gordon (36 games), Christian Braun (44) and Cameron Johnson (54) all posted strongly positive On-Off numbers but missed long stretches. The minutes they left went to Bruce Brown (-11 On-Off), Zeke Nnaji (-13.7) and Jonas Valančiūnas (-8.9), whose lineups gave ground.

The Minnesota series undid all of it. Denver took Game 1 at home 116-105, then dropped Game 2 at home 114-119 and was held to 96 in both games in Minnesota. It won Game 5 125-113 and fell 98-110 in Game 6. The offense that scored 122.07 a game in the regular season managed 107.5 in the playoffs. Its eFG % fell to 49.6 (12th of 16) and its 3P % to 31.1 (14th). Its offensive rebounding was the worst of any playoff team at 16.6 %, so the misses stayed misses. Murray's TS % dropped to 48.4 with a -11 On-Off. Jokić still posted an 8.0 BPM, but at a 55.4 TS %, far below his season. Getting to the line at the best FT Rate in the playoffs (36.2) wasn't enough to cover the shooting.

The longer view is less flattering than 54 wins suggests. Playoff wins have gone from 16 to 7 to 7 to 2. The offensive rating has climbed every year (117.6, 118.5, 119.9, 122.6), but the defensive rating has slid from 113.0 two years ago to 116.0 and now 117.4, ranked 21st in both of the last two seasons. Denver keeps building a better offense and a worse defense, and in a short series against a good defense that trade stopped working.

highlights.title: Best offense in the league
highlights.body: Denver led the league in offensive rating, eFG %, TS % and 3P %, and rarely turned it over. Jokić's creation drove it, and the rating has risen four straight seasons, so it is a durable identity rather than a hot year. The 39.6 % from three was a career-best level for this group and may not fully repeat.

highlights.title: Jokić at an MVP-level clip
highlights.body: Jokić posted a 14.2 BPM and 14.9 Win Shares on a 67 TS % while using over 30 % of possessions, and the team was 13.5 points per 100 better with him on the floor. He made the frontcourt the roster's only above-average group. As long as he plays, Denver starts from a very high floor.

highlights.title: A perfect regular-season finish
highlights.body: Denver won its last 10 games, including a 6-0 April, and outscored opponents by 10.5 a game over the stretch. That beat its season margin by 5.35 a game, so the run was carried by margin, not just close wins. It showed what the full rotation could do when healthy and set up the playoffs with momentum.

lowlights.title: Shooting collapse against Minnesota
lowlights.body: The playoff offense fell to a 49.6 eFG % and 31.1 % from three, and its 16.6 ORB % was the worst in the postseason, so there were no second chances. Murray's TS % sank to 48.4. Six games is a small sample and shooting swings are partly noise, but the poor offensive rebounding was already there in the regular season (24th).

lowlights.title: A defense that keeps slipping
lowlights.body: The 117.4 defensive rating ranked 21st for a second straight year, and Denver forced the fewest turnovers in the league. Opponents' 3-point shooting ranked third-lowest, which probably flattered the defense rather than reflecting a strength. Shooting guards scored freely against it, 26th in the league by points allowed to the position. The multi-year slide from a 113.0 rating makes this a structural problem, not a one-season dip.

lowlights.title: Bench minutes gave ground
lowlights.body: Gordon, Braun and Johnson all carried strong On-Off numbers but missed large chunks of the season. The players who absorbed their minutes graded poorly by On-Off: Brown at -11, Nnaji at -13.7 and Valančiūnas at -8.9. The C+ backcourt and wings grades reflect thin depth around the two stars.

arc.note: A strong November, a defensive leak in December, an offensive slump in January and a losing February gave way to a 10-0 finish, and then a six-game first-round exit.

recap.nextYear: The core that carries over is Jokić and Murray, the only two players producing well above average. The supporting cast with the best On-Off numbers (Gordon, Braun, Johnson) was positive when available but missed a lot of time, and the backcourt and wings both graded C+. Little of the 54 wins was luck: W vs Pt Diff was +1, so the record is a fair read of a team about five points per 100 better than average. The offense will likely stay elite, though the league-best 39.6 % from three has room to come down. The defense is the open question. It has ranked 21st two years running, rarely forces turnovers, and benefited from opponents' cold 3-point shooting. Add the weak offensive rebounding, which became the worst in the playoffs, and the needs are clear: defense and size around Jokić, not more scoring.

confidence.note: Full 82-game season with record matching margin; playoff read rests on six games.
